title: Rotate Array
prompt: Given an integer array `nums`, rotate the array to the right by `k` steps, where `k` is non-negative. Do this in place, using `O(1)` extra space beyond a few variables.

examples.explanation: k exceeds the array length, so it must first be reduced with k %= len(nums) (3 % 2 = 1), making this equivalent to a rotation by 1.

hints: Rotating one step at a time k times works but is O(n*k). Copying into a new array hits O(n) time but uses O(n) extra space — can you do it truly in place?
k can be larger than the array length, so the first move is always to reduce it: k %= len(nums).
A right rotation by k is the same as reversing the whole array, then reversing the first k elements, then reversing the remaining n-k elements — three reversals, each an O(1)-space two-pointer swap.

solution.approach: Normalize k with k %= len(nums) since rotating by the full length is a no-op. Then apply the reversal trick: reverse the entire array, which puts everything in the right relative rotated order but backward; then reverse the first k elements and the remaining n-k elements independently to fix each segment's internal order. Each reversal is a simple two-pointer swap done in place, so three linear-time reversals achieve the rotation in O(n) time and O(1) extra space, with no auxiliary array needed.
solution.code:
def rotate(nums, k):
    n = len(nums)
    k %= n

    def reverse(lo, hi):
        while lo < hi:
            nums[lo], nums[hi] = nums[hi], nums[lo]
            lo += 1
            hi -= 1

    reverse(0, n - 1)
    reverse(0, k - 1)
    reverse(k, n - 1)
    return nums
